_what: Where each app's conversations are on a person's computer, and how the import over the records door is paced: DATA read by read-data/chat-import.mjs, which names no app, no folder and no file. The folder the person grants (read-a-folder) is read as their home: every place here is a path under it, and nothing outside it is read. An account export is found by its file names under `export_places` (and the folders a run adds), `in_folder` (the folder it sits in, as Google Takeout names them) and `head_has` (words its first bytes hold, which tells two exports with one file name apart). A local AI app's sessions are found where its row of tools/keep-and-wake-ai-sessions-on-this-computer/harness/record-every-message.json says (`transcript_roots`, `~` being the granted folder) and read by that file's rules, the ones old Trillion recorded every message by. `reader` names how a file is read: chat-archive (read-data/chat-archives.mjs, an export of conversation trees), decode (read-data/decode_source.py with the sources.json row `decode_source`), harness (the harness rules). A new app is a new row here.

settings._what: most_text: the most characters one kept message part holds, so a part fits one door write (64 KiB); write_rows and write_bytes: one door write; retries, first_wait_ms, most_wait_ms: a busy or slow door (503, a timeout, an unknown outcome) is asked again with the same request key after a growing wait, this many times; call_timeout_ms: one door call; time_box_seconds: one run, after which it saves where it is and answers more: true; cursor_every: a file's cursor row is written after this many conversations; decode_page_atoms: one page of the decoder; head_bytes: how much of a file is read to tell what it is; cursor_bytes: the most a cursor row holds (rows a transcript is still waiting on are let go past it); transcript_read_bytes and transcript_row_bytes: one read of a session transcript and its largest row (the bounded older-transcript reader's own bounds).
settings._attachments: The files a message carried are copied into the person's files through the files door, under attachments_folder: an export's file as <attachments_folder>/<app>/<its name>, an image pasted into a session as <attachments_folder>/<conversation>/<message>-<n><extension> (old Trillion's own names for them). An export's files are looked for beside it, attachment_depth folders down, at most attachment_index_files files: a file whose name starts with the attachment's id (ChatGPT's file-XXXX-photo.png) or that sits in a folder named by it (Grok's prod-mc-asset-server/<id>/content). A file over most_attachment_bytes is counted, not copied. media_types names a file's media type by its extension; magic by the bytes it starts with (hex), for a file with no extension.
